trig.name: Step chance and conditions
device: MIDI Control Center accepted the update file; the unit restarted by itself and played existing patterns as before.
Chance (Randomness) and conditions (Probability) on SEQ1 and SEQ2 worked, and survived a save and a power cycle.
The inverted form reads clearly on the display as n12.
The update file, which has one more data frame than Arturia's, was accepted; the unit runs and the mod works.
trig.unchecked: Not yet reported from a device: swing, drum shift, reverse and alternate direction, changing pattern while playing, copy project, and long use.
guide: What it adds

Stock firmware plays every step that is on, every time the pattern comes round. This mod lets a single step play only some of the time, in one of two ways: by chance, or on chosen passes of the pattern.
A pass is one time through the pattern. With a 16-step pattern, pass 1 is the first 16 steps after you press Play, pass 2 is the next 16, and so on.
A step has a chance or a condition, not both. Steps you never touch play exactly as before.
Chance: hold a step and turn Randomness
The display shows a percentage. 100 is a normal step. 50 means the step plays about half the times it comes round, decided afresh each time; 25 about one time in four.
The values run from 1 to 99 in 21 stages, closer together near the two ends.
With no step held, Randomness is the normal track control.
Conditions: hold a step and turn Probability

A condition makes the step play on fixed passes, so the result repeats exactly. Turning right walks through them in this order: 1-1, 1St, n1S, 1-2, n12, 2-2, n22, 1-3, n13, 2-3, n23, 3-3, n33, 1-4, n14, 2-4, n24, 3-4, n34, 4-4, n44.
1-1 is no condition: the step always plays.

A-B means: count the passes in groups of B, and play only on pass A of each group. 1-2 plays on passes 1, 3, 5, 7 and so on. 2-2 plays on passes 2, 4, 6, 8. 1-4 plays on passes 1, 5, 9. 4-4 plays on passes 4, 8, 12.
The n forms are the opposite of the same numbers: nAB plays on every pass except the one A-B would play. n14 plays on passes 2, 3, 4, then 6, 7, 8. n44 plays on passes 1, 2, 3, then 5, 6, 7.
1St plays on the first pass after Play only. n1S plays on every pass but the first.
With no step held, Probability is the normal track control.
What you can do with it
A fill at the end of every fourth bar: put the fill's steps on 4-4.
A pattern longer than its steps: a 16-step pattern with some steps on 1-2 and others on 2-2 is a 32-step phrase. With 1-4 to 4-4 it is a 64-step phrase in 16 steps.
An intro that never comes back: 1St. A part that enters after the first time round: n1S.
Hi-hats or ghost notes that vary: a chance of 50 to 75.
Ratchets: hold a drum step and touch the roller strip
A ratchet makes one step play several times inside its own length: 2, 4 or 8 quick hits where there was one. It gives you a 1/32 roll on a 1/16 track without changing the track's step size.

On the DRUM track, hold a step that is on and touch the strip at a rate finer than the track's step size. On a 1/16 track, 1/32 gives 2 hits. On a 1/8 track, 1/16 gives 2 and 1/32 gives 4. On a 1/4 track you can have 2, 4 or 8.
The display shows r 2, r 4 or r 8. Touching the strip at the track's own rate, or a coarser one, removes the ratchet: r 1.
Ratcheted steps light cyan in place of the track's purple.
Recording: with Record on, a roll that is finer than the track marks each step it fills with at least two hits.
All hits have the step's velocity. The step's gate is taken of the gap between hits, so every hit ends before the next.
A step's chance or condition is decided once, for all of its hits.
A drum pattern holds up to 96 ratcheted steps; the display shows FuL at the limit.
Turning Swing while a drum step is held shows the step's ratchet and leaves the swing alone.
Ratchets do not play while the looper is repeating steps.
Passes are counted per track
Counting starts at 1 when you press Play from stop, and again when the pattern changes.
SEQ1 and SEQ2 each count their own passes, so tracks of different lengths drift against each other as they already do.
On the DRUM track the step buttons belong to the selected pad, and so do the chance and condition you set. Each pad counts the passes of its own length.
In alternate direction, a pass is there and back.
Good to know
Chance and conditions are saved with the pattern when you save the project.
Turning a step off removes its chance or condition. So do the stock functions that shift or copy steps. Copying a pattern or a project keeps them.
Arturia's own firmware ignores them: a pattern saved with the mod plays every step again after you go back to stock.
trig.summary: Each SEQ1, SEQ2 and DRUM step can have a chance to play (hold the step, turn Randomness) or a condition such as every second pass (hold the step, turn Probability).
changes: Recording: a hit recorded over a rolled step now always removes its ratchet. 1.3.0 followed only the roller's own hits, one of the ten places a recorded hit comes from; it was never installed on a device.

Ratchets on DRUM steps: a step can play 2, 4 or 8 times inside its own length. Hold a step and touch the roller strip at a rate finer than the track to set it, at the track's rate or coarser to clear it; recording a finer roll sets it too. Ratcheted steps light cyan. Up to 96 per drum pattern, saved with it.
Chance and conditions on DRUM steps too, set on the selected pad's steps and saved with the drum pattern. Each pad counts the passes of its own length. Copy project carries them.

Step conditions on SEQ1 and SEQ2: hold a step and turn Probability. 1-1 is none, 1St and n1S are first pass only and not first pass, A-B plays on pass A of every B, nAB on every pass but that one, for B up to 4.
The chance of a held step is now set with the Randomness knob. Probability is left as stock, kept for per-step conditions.
First version: per-step trigger chance, saved with the pattern.

dump.name: Bootloader dump
dump.summary: Sends the bootloader over USB MIDI when Probability is turned. A one-off tool, not for playing.
changes: Fix: 1.0.0 sent the dump out of the 5-pin MIDI output instead of USB. Now sent over USB, and a message the USB queue refuses is sent again.
